:::{#exm-expression}
#### Two expressions for one function

The [expressions](#def-expression) $a x^2 + b x + c$ and $(a x + b)\,x + c$
[denote](#def-denotes) the same [function](functions.qmd#def-function) of $x$ for any fixed $a$, $b$ and $c$,
because they give the same value at every $x$.

Precedence parses $a x^2 + b x + c$ as a sum of three terms:
the power $x^2$ is applied first,
then $a$ multiplies $x^2$ and $b$ multiplies $x$,
and the three products are added.
The parentheses in $(a x + b)\,x + c$ force a different tree:
$a$ multiplies $x$, $b$ is added, the sum multiplies $x$,
and $c$ is added.

:::
